video_title: REACTION: Dybantsa VS. Peterson In Blockbuster Top Battle

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Evaluating the Summer League performance of AJ Dybantsa and Darren Peterson
quotes.excerpt: I thought it was good work by both of them.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: Considering what I've seen from rookies in their first games, I thought it was good work by both of them. It was a four-point game, but it really was lopsided. The Wizards won, the Jazz closed it late. I'm a little bit concerned because Dybantsa looked like he was holding his calf at the end of the game.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim MacMahon
text_blocks.text: I'm hoping, and I'm not trying to be funny or ironic here, I'm hoping it was just a cramp. Listen, I know there's been a lot of whining and crying about the little free throw rule, the one for either two or three, whatever it is. Thank God that exists in this game or we'd have been up way past midnight.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: AJ Dybantsa's impressive all-around game and physical first step
quotes.excerpt: I thought he showed a pretty good all-around game, Dybantsa, and especially a quick first step.
quotes.quote: AJ Dybantsa had 27 points, seven rebounds, two steals and a block. He was seven of 18 from the field. He really shot the ball poorly outside, but what I was impressed with, first off, he tied a record. He tied with Blake Griffin for the most points scored for a number one overall pick in his Summer League debut. I think he's up there with John Wall and some other guys who had that many points in their first game. I thought he showed a pretty good all-around game, Dybantsa, and especially a quick first step, which is one of the reasons he kept getting fouled. He got fouled eight times and he got most of his points at the foul line.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Darren Peterson's elite athleticism and potential as a shooter
quotes.excerpt: He is a physical athletic specimen from the second that he stepped in to the league.
quotes.quote: He is an amazing athlete. He had one driving dunk, he had a couple other finishes through contact. Some of the shots that he missed, including one against Peterson, he's going to be able to get to that little off-dribble spin turnaround whenever he wants and he creates a lot of space with that. He's only going to get better as a shooter as he obviously gets more reps and matures. But man, he is a physical athletic specimen from the second that he stepped in to the league.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: AJ Dybantsa's efficiency and physical development
quotes.excerpt: He played 26 minutes. He had one turnover and he was bringing the ball up a little bit.
quotes.quote: He played 26 minutes. He had one turnover and he was bringing the ball up a little bit. He had one turnover and one foul. He is at his best from the mid-range. He's really got a great mid-range game. The long game has to develop a little bit as this game showed, but he's going to score from day one.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Trey Johnson's impressive Summer League debut as a lottery pick
quotes.excerpt: Trey Johnson, lottery pick from the 2025 draft, he looked pretty good tonight.
quotes.quote: I should point out that Trey Johnson, lottery pick from the 2025 draft, he looked pretty good tonight. He looked like a set, you want your lottery picks, your second year lottery picks, you want them to be impressive. Trey Johnson was impressive, 11 of 20 shooting, 26 points. Didn't shoot the ball well from three, but generated space and got in there. That should be a good first impression there from the Wizards.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Darren Peterson's inefficient shooting night and defensive struggles
quotes.excerpt: Nine fouls, he was one foul away from the dreaded 10 foul, you're out, Summer League rule.
quotes.quote: Not a great shooting night for him and nine fouls. He was one foul away from the dreaded 10 foul, you're out, Summer League rule, and eight turnovers in 30 minutes. The Jazz definitely were into him a little bit more, trying to be physical with him defensively, and it resulted in him having a very inefficient night. Six of 18 shooting. He threw in like a 30-footer at the buzzer to get himself to 24 points. Still liked the way he generated open shots like we saw in Salt Lake, they just weren't going in as much.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamir Watkins' physical defense on Darren Peterson
quotes.excerpt: Jamir Watkins also had nine fouls and a lot of those were regarding Peterson.
quotes.quote: Jamir Watkins also had nine fouls and a lot of those were regarding Peterson. Clearly he was like, hey, I got ten to play with and he was just being physical 94 feet with him. Peterson's had an eight turnover game now, a two turnover game and a nine turnover game. There's a couple things there. Number one, he's more of a two than a one, and he's going to be sharing the backcourt with Keyonte George. He's going to be sharing ball handling and initiating responsibilities. Keyonte George will take more of those than Peterson is going to take early on.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Darren Peterson's role as a shooting guard rather than point guard
quotes.excerpt: He's really a shooting guard who can make really good reads and really good passes.
quotes.quote: He's really a shooting guard who can make really good reads and really good passes than he is a guy who you want bringing the ball up the floor at this point in his career. You could see how easy it is for him to create space in the half court. He missed some threes that were off-dribble threes that he did a great job creating space, and he's got really good footwork, way above the norm footwork for a 19, 20-year-old.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Darren Peterson's likely conclusion to his Summer League participation
quotes.excerpt: I don't know this for certain, but he might be done for Summer League.
quotes.quote: I don't know this for certain, but he might be done for Summer League. Typically these high lottery picks only play two or three games now, so that might have been it for him.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Wizards roster players attending Summer League games
quotes.excerpt: All 11 Wizards who were on their roster players who were not on the Summer League team.
quotes.quote: I think they said on the broadcast that all 11 Wizards who were on their roster players who were not on the Summer League team were at the game tonight.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: The Wizards' and Jazz's pressure to improve and contend
quotes.excerpt: There's real pressure on the front office and the coach in Washington that there's not in Utah.
quotes.quote: I'll put it like this, there's real pressure on the front office and the coach in Washington that there's not in Utah.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Quinn Snyder's appearance at Summer League in Salt Lake City
quotes.excerpt: I saw Quinn Snyder in Salt Lake City and man, he looked fresh and rested and relaxed.
quotes.quote: I saw Quinn Snyder in Salt Lake City and man, he looked fresh and rested and relaxed. So I just saw Summer Quinn, we're about to see Summer Windy.
